NONE: › to cause something to happen in a violent and often uncontrolled way
造成，引起（災禍等）

example: The recent storms have wreaked havoc on crops.
最近的暴風雨給農作物造成了巨大災害。
She was determined to wreak revenge/vengeance on both him and his family.
她決心要報復他和他的家人。

NONE: › an arrangement of flowers and leaves in a circular shape, used as a decoration or as a sign of respect and remembrance for a person who has died
花環；花圈

example: a holly/laurel wreath
聖誕冬青花環／桂冠
The bride wore a veil with a wreath of silk flowers.
新娘戴著一塊飾有絲綢花環的面紗。
There were two large wreaths on the coffin.
棺材上擺放著兩個巨大的花圈。
The president ended his visit by laying a wreath at the war memorial.
總統向戰爭紀念碑敬獻了花圈，以此結束自己的訪問。

NONE: › to cover or surround something
覆蓋；纏繞，環繞

example: The peak of the mountain is perpetually wreathed in cloud.
這座山的山頂長年雲霧繚繞。

NONE: C2 to destroy or badly damage something
破壞；毀壞
› informal to spoil something completely
毀掉；完全破壞
C2 a vehicle or ship that has been destroyed or badly damaged
嚴重損毀的交通工具；沉船
C2 informal someone who is in bad physical or mental condition
健康（或精神）嚴重受損的人

example: The explosion shattered nearby windows and wrecked two cars.
爆炸震碎了附近的窗子，並毀壞了兩輛汽車。
Our greenhouse was wrecked in last night's storm.
我們的溫室在昨晚的暴風雨中遭到破壞。
He has been warned that his behaviour might wreck his chances of promotion.
有人警告他說，他的行為可能會毀掉自己晉升的機會。
Divers exploring the wreck managed to salvage some coins and jewellery.
探尋沉船的潛水員設法打撈到一些硬幣和珠寶。
The burned-out wrecks of two police cars littered the road.
路上遍佈著兩輛被燒毀警車的殘骸。
The stress she had been under at work reduced her to a nervous/quivering wreck.
工作上的壓力令她非常緊張／戰戰兢兢。

NONE: C2 a badly damaged object or the separated parts of a badly damaged object
嚴重受損的東西；殘骸
› what is left of something that has been spoiled or that has failed
剩餘物；殘存物

example: Two children were trapped in the wreckage.
兩名兒童被困在殘骸裡。
The wreckage of the car was scattered over the roadside.
那輛汽車的殘骸散落在路旁。
Kate was still clinging to the wreckage of her failed marriage.
凱特仍然執著於她那破碎的婚姻，不想放手。

NONE: › very badly damaged
遭到嚴重破壞的；被毀的

example: Just look at what you've done to my coat - it's wrecked.
看看你對我的大衣做的好事——它全毀了。
He got completely wrecked last Saturday night.
上週六晚，他醉得一塌糊塗。

NONE: › a
tow truck
› a large, heavy metal ball that is swung against a building in order to knock it down because it is no longer needed
（拆除房屋等用的）落錘
› a very small, brown bird
鷦鷯
› a member of the British Women's Royal Naval Service
英國皇家海軍婦女服務隊隊員

T + adv/prep: › [ T + adv/prep ] to pull and twist something suddenly or violently away from its position
T: › [ T ] to twist part of your body badly, such as your arm or leg, and injure it
T usually passive: › [ T usually passive ] to suddenly take someone from people they love, causing them great unhappiness

C: › [ C ] mainly US a tool for holding and turning objects, especially one that can be made larger and smaller to hold different sized objects

C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] a sudden, violent twist or pull

S: › [ S ] a feeling of unhappiness when you have to leave a person or place that you love
（被迫離開某人或某地時的）痛苦，難受

example: The photographer tripped over the cord, wrenching a microphone from its stand.
攝影師被一根電線絆了一下，將一支麥克風從底座上猛扯了下來。
The phone had been wrenched from/off the wall.
電話從牆上被猛地扯了下來。
The ball was wrenched out of his grasp by another player.
球被另一名球員從他手中猛地搶了過去。
His hands were tied but he managed to wrench himself free.
他雙手被綁，但他設法掙脫開來。
He wrenched his right shoulder during a game of hockey.
他在一場曲棍球比賽中扭傷了自己的右肩。
At the age of eight, she was wrenched from her foster parents and sent to live with another family.
八歲時，她被人從養父母身邊奪走，送去與另一家人一起生活。
an adjustable wrench
活動扳手
See also
monkey wrench
She found leaving home a real wrench.
她發現離開家是一件非常痛苦的事。

NONE: › extremely stressful
極為痛苦的，極為難受的

example: It was the most wrenching decision of the president’s life.
這是總統一生中作出的最痛苦的決定。

NONE: › formal to get something with effort or difficulty
辛苦謀求；費力取得
› to violently pull something away from someone
奪取；攫取

example: The shareholders are planning to wrest control of the company (away) from the current directors.
股東們正在計劃從現任董事手中奪取公司的控制權。
He wrested the letter from my grasp.
他從我手中奪走了那封信。

NONE: › to fight with someone (especially as a sport) by holding them and trying to throw them to the ground
（尤指作為運動）（與…）摔跤，角力；（將…）摔倒

example: He has wrestled professionally for five years.
他從事職業摔跤已有五年了。
The police officer tackled the man and wrestled him to the ground.
員警揪住那個人，並把他摔倒在地。

NONE: › to try very hard to deal with a problem or to make a difficult decision
努力解決；艱難對付

example: The government is wrestling with difficult economic problems.
政府正在努力應對嚴重的經濟問題。
He wrestled with the decision for several weeks, wondering what he should do.
他為作這個決定苦苦思索了幾個星期，不知道該如何是好。

NONE: › a person who wrestles as a sport
摔跤運動員
› a sport in which two people fight and try to throw each other to the ground
摔跤運動

C: › a person who experiences something unpleasant
› informal or humorous someone who is unpleasant or annoying
討厭的人；無恥之徒；惡棍

example: a poor/miserable wretch
可憐的／悲慘的人
Who trampled on my flowers? I bet it was those two little wretches who live next door.
誰踩了我的花？我敢肯定是住在隔壁的那兩個小壞蛋。
You wretch! You promised you'd give me a lift.
你真討厭！你答應過讓我搭車的。

NONE: C2 unpleasant or of low quality
苦惱的；不幸的；素質差的
C2 very ill or very unhappy
病得厲害的；不愉快的
› UK used to express anger when something annoying happens
（表示憎惡）討厭的，該死的

example: a wretched childhood
不幸的童年
The people live in wretched conditions, with no running water.
人們的居住條件非常糟糕，沒有自來水。
I think I must be coming down with flu - I've been feeling wretched all day.
我覺得我定是得流感了——我一整天都很不舒服。
My wretched car's broken down again.
我那該死的車又拋錨了。

NONE: › extremely, when referring to something unpleasant or of low quality
極其地，極端地
